points: This perek continues the vision of the Beis HaMikdash. Last perek showed avodah zarah; this one shows murder, the second of the three cardinal sins for which the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed.
Six armed men come with a scribe and are told to kill everyone in the city, men, women and children, and pile the corpses in the Beis HaMikdash, bringing tumah into it.
The root of the murder: they believed Hashem no longer watched or cared, and that led to a dark path. Because they thought Hashem left, the kavod Hashem leaves the Beis HaMikdash.
The scribe marks those who groaned at society's breakdown, and they are saved. Those who sinned and those who stayed silent are punished. If wrongdoing doesn't move you, something is broken.
A man from Meah Shearim whispered "Shabbos" at every passing car so he would never become desensitized. If we can't change what's wrong, we must at least groan, keeping our moral compass intact.
